description: Researchers at the Fraunhofer Institute for Integrated Circuits IIS publish GNSS interference datasets on IEEE DataPort for detecting and classifying jamming. The GNSS Spectrum Highway Datasets 1 and 2 hold spectral snapshots recorded by the institute's own sensor station beside a German motorway, labelled in eight interference classes and three non-interference classes, which capture real in-vehicle jammers passing by (baseline accuracy 97.66 percent). Further sets give controlled low-frequency interference spectra and processed interference features from short-time Fourier transforms with statistical measures (2023, Feather format). Coverage: one motorway site in Germany and laboratory scenarios, 2022 to 2024. Format and access: NumPy arrays and Feather files; these are standard datasets on IEEE DataPort, where the page shows a subscriber notice, so downloading needs an IEEE DataPort subscription; the licence is CC BY 4.0 according to DataCite. Caveats: spectra and features, not raw samples for positioning; one site; labels from the authors. Simulation uses: rates and types of real-world jamming near roads for hazard exposure of GNSS-dependent traffic and timing systems, and training of detectors. Related records: Jammertest and OAKBAT give controlled attacks; GPSJam shows regional interference from aircraft reports.
